doc.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

chapter: New York, the clarinet and first gigs
title: Vocal lessons in New York and 'All the Things You Are'
summary: After the move to New York his mother put him in a Broadway vocal studio; talk turns to the difficulty of 'All the Things You Are'.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I did a little something, but he caught me on it. And to myself I said well I don’t care what he thinks, it sounds okay to me. But so he was musical so there must have been some musical feeling on my father’s side, on my father’s side of the family. Time went by, we moved to New York, and my mother I guess was a show biz mother in her own way, you never figure to think about it, but we came to New York and she somehow found a studio or something that gave kids vocal lessons and it was on Broadway — getting to the big time — Broadway, 52nd, 51st, 53rd Street. You go upstairs you know, and I went up there was a woman, and I don’t know whether she played the piano or whether it was a guy that played the piano, and we sang songs. And I remember I had the sheet music for [sings] You are the promised kiss of springtime — you know that thing.
So I sang through that. So I mean isn’t that funny, I had to re-learn that many a time.
Do we need to stop, Tim? TH: Yes, please. I need to move this. When you shift you’re getting pinched here and I’m going to bring this around the others side.
Yeah I mean it’s got very nice changes, but you’ve really got to know them. I’ve been on the rocks more than once with it.
At Jimmy Ryan’s. I mean Bobby Pratt, the wonderful trombone player and piano player, he played the hell out of it with Roy Eldridge you know like that, he knew the sucker. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
Right. So you did “All the Things You Are.” It does have that, getting about halfway through it’s got that —
Oh yeah, yeah [scats] it goes somewhere else.
Are we on the air? TH: Yup.
